subject: Biotechnology
title: Gene Therapy Biologics
description: A quick, practical guide to Gene Therapy Biologics.

hook.text: Zolgensma costs $2.1 million per dose — it is a one-time gene therapy that saves babies from fatal paralysis.

buildup.text: An AAV vector delivers a working copy of the SMN1 gene — motor neurons start producing the survival protein.

discovery.text: Babies treated before symptoms appear develop almost normally — early treatment is the key to maximum benefit.

twist.text: Manufacturing AAV at scale is a bottleneck — each dose requires trillions of viral particles, produced in huge batches.

climax.text: Over 20 gene therapy products are approved worldwide — a new class of biologics is becoming mainstream medicine.

punchline.text: One dose, one gene, one cure — gene therapy biologics rewrite the rules.

quiz.question: Why must Zolgensma be given early in a baby's life?
options: The AAV vector only works in immature immune systems
Motor neurons die progressively, so early treatment preserves more neurons for normal development
The gene only functions during the first year of life

details.summary: Gene therapy biologics deliver functional genes to patients with genetic diseases, providing potentially curative one-time treatments. Approved products like Zolgensma for spinal muscular atrophy and Luxturna for inherited blindness represent milestones in treating previously untreatable conditions.
details.whyItMatters: Gene therapy fulfills biotechnology's original promise of treating disease at the genetic level. Single treatments costing millions generate debate about healthcare economics but offer cures for devastating diseases that previously had no treatment
takeaways: Gene therapy delivers functional genes to correct genetic diseases
Zolgensma at 2.1 million dollars was the most expensive drug at launch
One-time treatments may be more cost-effective than lifelong alternatives

faq.question: How is a gene therapy drug different from a traditional medicine?
faq.answer: Traditional drugs treat symptoms with ongoing doses. Gene therapy delivers a functional copy of a defective gene using a viral vector, enabling the patient's own cells to produce the missing protein permanently. One treatment can potentially cure the underlying genetic cause.

faq.question: Why does Zolgensma cost over two million dollars?
faq.answer: Development costs exceeded a billion dollars for a drug treating only about 500 new patients annually in the US. Manufacturing requires massive quantities of viral vector with stringent quality. The company argues it replaces millions in lifetime treatment costs for spinal muscular atrophy.
